rationale: This is the archive's strongest signal (Profitable Inventory Divergence) with the now-formulaic NEG(DELTA(che)) third leg bolted on — a template already applied four separate times in the archive (Liquidity-Depleting Post-Peak Expansion, Liquidity-Funded Expansion Breadth, Distressed Working-Capital Substitution, Liquidity-Draining Replacement Trap) — so it is a cosmetic extension rather than a new mechanism, and MIN-narrowing a leg that already delivers t=-4.9 is more likely to dilute than sharpen.

Identical construction pattern to the previous proposal — Tangible Expansion Crowds Out Innovation plus the reused cash-depletion leg — and no argument is offered for why liquidity strain is economically distinct from the capex-increase leg it is being conjoined with (rising capex mechanically drains cash), so the third leg risks being redundant rather than informative.

The reasoning correctly diagnoses the strong-slope/weak-alpha problem of Profitable Expansion Breadth as CMA overlap and substitutes a realized-payoff-failure leg rather than another liquidity leg, though the resulting expression is close to Profitable Inventory Divergence with a ppegt leg appended, so incremental information over the archive's best signal is uncertain.

The margin-trend leg has already been directly tested in Fixed-Capacity Margin Squeeze and was essentially dead (fmb -0.05, ls_talpha 0.28), and adding a third leg to Capex Without Capacity Formation was already tried (Liquidity-Draining Replacement Trap) with no gain, so this combines two known-unhelpful modifications and will most likely just shrink the sample.

Same reused cash-depletion-leg template applied to a weak base (Inventory-Backed Margin Inflation, fmb -1.78, ls_talpha -0.90), and the hypothesis is internally strained because the overproduction story implies margins rise from cost deferral while cash falls from inventory build — two symptoms of the same accounting event, not independent confirmation.

This is a genuinely distinct two-leg mechanism (purchased versus internally developed innovation) that is not a rediscovery of any archive signal and whose expected negative sign follows naturally from both legs, with the caveats that COALESCE-to-zero makes non-R&D reporters indistinguishable from true R&D cutters and that aqc's sparsity may limit coverage.
